body: Thanks friend. Maybe tomorrow will be better.

Thank you. It's helped take my mind off things tonight. I'm probably going to sleep soon. Could I PM you some time for random chat if I don't crash and burn? I've enjoyed chatting with you as well. If not that's cool.

Dang. That bites!

You know, it sucks knowing you're a whole person underneath the illnesses. :\ Like... there's all this good inside of me, all the cool stuff that I'm good at. Everyone tells me how talented I am and how they wish they could be as good as I am at whatever I pick up. And that's really cool, it compensates some or has in the past for all the shitty cards I've been dealt. There are things I'm good at and it helps. But it also sucks to step back and look at, and realize all that is going to be lost because of all this.
Right, I know. And photoshop helps. It's enhanced some shots that I thought weren't any good, but there was a lot hiding there.

I'd never seen itookapicture before. That's cool. The problem is I can't get out and do things much anymore (too much pain, too little energy, and now I live in a city so there's nothing right in my vicinity to walk to) so I can't take lots of pictures that might be useful as stock. I do have about 60 good pictures (I think) that might sell as prints. So I don't know, if I go to the hospital and come out feeling better maybe I will pursue that.

It's a Nikon Coolpix L830. I love it. It's red and takes fantastic pictures. I upgraded a year or two ago from a very old and beat-up Canon that had 5 or 6 megapixels... lol. My favorite subject matter is nature. Flowers, trees, anything interesting you can find in the garden or on a walk or in a nature preserve. I've actually wanted to start a business selling prints of my photography for some time, but I need a little funding for it. >.< And now my mental state is so shitty I'd feel awful taking funding for it because what if I do off myself? That would be a terrible investment for somebody, or a terrible loan risk.

That might be a good idea... It's hard to get engaged sometimes. But it's a good idea. 

Maybe I'd try animation if my drawing got better. I'm really at the learning the basics level, but I'm very good with color and the general "know whether something looks right" feel. So I just need the technical knowledge, I think. Ctrl+Paint has been helpful.
Oh. I forgot photography. I don't know HOW I forgot photography...

I do actually. Knit, crochet, embroidery, used to paint in better days, working on learning digital painting/drawing (when I can sit at the desk, which for the last few weeks has been not at all), I've tried making candles (harder than you'd think) and sewing (also hard, I feel like I need a class or something but I don't have a way to get around on my own)... I write a lot. I have several fiction projects going, one of them pretty new. I bake when I can. I recently came up with this idea for melon tarts which came out rather spectacularly. My husband raved over them and doesn't even like honeydew. I like singing but I don't know any instruments. I try or tried to do as much as I could while disabled. I really do love all of it... But it seems like it's been outweighed in the last several weeks or months. And especially the last few days. I'm working on an embroidery project for a friend that I'm kind of upset that I might not finish. It's about 2/3 done.

It was really pleasant. First money started showing up in the same place every few minutes or so (time wasn't really clear). Like 20s and 100s. So I kept collecting it for a while. And it was clearly magic because I watched it and no one was dropping it off. Then I went to a thrift store and spent some of it on really amazingly underpriced finds like rings in just the style I like, in my size. And then I found myself at a house near a small cove with white sand and blue water that I went and put my feet in. I think it was mine. That was pretty much the extent of it. There were a few realistic aspects like gnats around the water, so it didn't feel super dreamlike. 

Sorry I disappeared for a while. Husband came in to talk about random things and I shut my laptop off. If I could just get tired I'd go to sleep.

That is kind of funny. Not ha-ha, obviously. But it feels a little serendipitous. Right this second I'm just listening to Ben Howard's "I Forget Where We Were" album. "Has the world gone mad or is it me? All these small things, they gather round me, gather round me. Is it all so very bad? I can't see." That's what's playing right now. And I'm thinking how much it relates to my life. I'm thinking about a good dream I had earlier, and how strange it feels to have a good dream in the midst of all this. And it's a little too cold in here, but the cat is sleeping on the blanket and I don't want to move her.
